15. # Template Comparison
16. 
17. This skill helps an agent compare 2+ `dotnet new` templates side by side so the user can
18. pick the right one. It inspects each template's parameters and feature support and renders
19. a comparison table.
20. 
21. ## When to Use
22. 
23. - User is deciding between similar templates (e.g., `webapi` vs `webapp`, `blazor` vs `blazorwasm`)
24. - User asks "which template should I use for X?"
25. - User wants to understand how two or more templates differ before creating a project
26. 
27. ## When Not to Use
28. 
29. - User wants to create a project — route to `template-instantiation`
30. - User wants to author or validate a custom template — route to `template-authoring` or `template-validation`
31. - User just needs to find or inspect a single template — route to `template-discovery`
32. 
33. ## Inputs
34. 
35. | Input | Required | Description |
36. |-------|----------|-------------|
37. | Template short names | Yes | Two or more template short names to compare (e.g., `webapi`, `webapp`) |
38. | Comparison focus | No | Optional aspect to emphasize (auth, AOT, frameworks, interactivity) |
39. 
40. ## Workflow
41. 
42. ### Step 1: Inspect each template
43. 
44. Run `dotnet new <template> --help` for each template being compared to collect its
45. parameters (names, types, defaults, choices) and supported frameworks:
46. 
47. ```bash
48. dotnet new webapi --help
49. dotnet new webapp --help
50. ```
51. 
52. If a template is not installed, find and install it first (`dotnet new search <keyword>`,
53. then `dotnet new install <package>`).
54. 
55. > **Run `--help` calls sequentially.** The template engine uses a global mutex, so running
56. > several `dotnet new <template> --help` commands concurrently can fail with a transient
57. > "mutex"/"persistence" error and empty output. Inspect templates one at a time; if a call
58. > fails, retry it once before moving on, and still produce the comparison from whatever
59. > parameter knowledge you have rather than ending with no answer.
60. 
61. ### Step 2: Build the comparison table
62. 
63. Produce a side-by-side table covering:
64. 
65. - **Parameters** — name, type, default, choices
66. - **Feature support** — auth, AOT, Docker, controllers, interactivity
67. - **Available frameworks** — e.g., net8.0, net9.0, net10.0
68. - **Classifications** — categories the template advertises (Web, API, Blazor, etc.)
69. 
70. Example shape:
71. 
72. | Aspect | `webapi` | `webapp` |
73. |--------|----------|----------|
74. | Auth (`--auth`) | None, Individual, SingleOrg, Windows | None, Individual, SingleOrg, ... |
75. | AOT (`--aot` flag) | n/a — native AOT via publish-time `PublishAot` | n/a |
76. | Controllers (`--use-controllers`) | Yes | n/a |
77. | Interactivity | n/a | n/a |
78. | Frameworks | net8.0 / net9.0 / net10.0 | net8.0 / net9.0 / net10.0 |
79. | Classifications | Web, WebAPI | Web, Razor Pages |
80. 
81. ### Step 3: Recommend
82. 
83. Summarize the key differences and recommend a template for the user's stated scenario,
84. linking to `template-instantiation` to create it.
85. 
86. ## Validation
87. 
88. - [ ] Every template requested was inspected via `dotnet new <template> --help`
89. - [ ] The comparison covers parameters, feature support, frameworks, and classifications
90. - [ ] Differences relevant to the user's scenario are called out explicitly
91. - [ ] A recommendation (or clear trade-off) is provided
92. 
93. ## Common Pitfalls
94. 
95. | Pitfall | Solution |
96. |---------|----------|
97. | Comparing uninstalled templates from memory | Install and inspect each template so the comparison reflects the real parameters and choices. |
98. | Assuming feature parity | Parameter names and feature support vary by template — confirm each with `--help`. |
99. | Comparing fundamentally different template types | Only compare templates that solve overlapping problems; note when they target different scenarios. |
100. 
101. ## More Info
102. 
103. - [dotnet new templates](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-new-sdk-templates) — built-in template reference
104. - [dotnet new](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-new) — CLI reference
105.

 # Template Comparison
 
 This skill helps an agent compare 2+ `dotnet new` templates side by side so the user can
 pick the right one. It inspects each template's parameters and feature support and renders
 a comparison table.
 
 ## When to Use
 
 - User is deciding between similar templates (e.g., `webapi` vs `webapp`, `blazor` vs `blazorwasm`)
 - User asks "which template should I use for X?"
 - User wants to understand how two or more templates differ before creating a project
 
 ## When Not to Use
 
 - User wants to create a project — route to `template-instantiation`
 - User wants to author or validate a custom template — route to `template-authoring` or `template-validation`
 - User just needs to find or inspect a single template — route to `template-discovery`
 
 ## Inputs
 
 | Input | Required | Description |
 |-------|----------|-------------|
 | Template short names | Yes | Two or more template short names to compare (e.g., `webapi`, `webapp`) |
 | Comparison focus | No | Optional aspect to emphasize (auth, AOT, frameworks, interactivity) |
 
 ## Workflow
 
 ### Step 1: Inspect each template
 
 Run `dotnet new <template> --help` for each template being compared to collect its
 parameters (names, types, defaults, choices) and supported frameworks:
 
 ```bash
 dotnet new webapi --help
 dotnet new webapp --help
 ```
 
 If a template is not installed, find and install it first (`dotnet new search <keyword>`,
 then `dotnet new install <package>`).
 
 > **Run `--help` calls sequentially.** The template engine uses a global mutex, so running
 > several `dotnet new <template> --help` commands concurrently can fail with a transient
 > "mutex"/"persistence" error and empty output. Inspect templates one at a time; if a call
 > fails, retry it once before moving on, and still produce the comparison from whatever
 > parameter knowledge you have rather than ending with no answer.
 
 ### Step 2: Build the comparison table
 
 Produce a side-by-side table covering:
 
 - **Parameters** — name, type, default, choices
 - **Feature support** — auth, AOT, Docker, controllers, interactivity
 - **Available frameworks** — e.g., net8.0, net9.0, net10.0
 - **Classifications** — categories the template advertises (Web, API, Blazor, etc.)
 
 Example shape:
 
 | Aspect | `webapi` | `webapp` |
 |--------|----------|----------|
 | Auth (`--auth`) | None, Individual, SingleOrg, Windows | None, Individual, SingleOrg, ... |
 | AOT (`--aot` flag) | n/a — native AOT via publish-time `PublishAot` | n/a |
 | Controllers (`--use-controllers`) | Yes | n/a |
 | Interactivity | n/a | n/a |
 | Frameworks | net8.0 / net9.0 / net10.0 | net8.0 / net9.0 / net10.0 |
 | Classifications | Web, WebAPI | Web, Razor Pages |
 
 ### Step 3: Recommend
 
 Summarize the key differences and recommend a template for the user's stated scenario,
 linking to `template-instantiation` to create it.
 
 ## Validation
 
 - [ ] Every template requested was inspected via `dotnet new <template> --help`
 - [ ] The comparison covers parameters, feature support, frameworks, and classifications
 - [ ] Differences relevant to the user's scenario are called out explicitly
 - [ ] A recommendation (or clear trade-off) is provided
 
 ## Common Pitfalls
 
 | Pitfall | Solution |
 |---------|----------|
 | Comparing uninstalled templates from memory | Install and inspect each template so the comparison reflects the real parameters and choices. |
 | Assuming feature parity | Parameter names and feature support vary by template — confirm each with `--help`. |
 | Comparing fundamentally different template types | Only compare templates that solve overlapping problems; note when they target different scenarios. |
 
 ## More Info
 
 - [dotnet new templates](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-new-sdk-templates) — built-in template reference
 - [dotnet new](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-new) — CLI reference
